ckpt_corruption_incident_20260810.what_happened: the FIRST step220000.pt was truncated to 5,956,287,104 B of 12,181,311,650 B (48.9%) and torch.load fails with 'PytorchStreamReader failed finding central directory'. Quarantined on .73 as step220000.pt.CORRUPT_truncated_49pct_watcher_race -- NOT deleted, it is the evidence.
ckpt_corruption_incident_20260810.root_cause: BOTH watchers used a ready-test that a partially-written file passes. torch.save creates the file and then streams 12.18 GB into it. Trainer-side (scripts/_run_a03_arm4_peaklr.sh) used bare `[ -f ]` -> fired 8s after the step line, SIGTERM + sleep 20 + kill -9 at +28s; a 12.18 GB save cannot finish in 28 s on this FS. Eval-side (.82) used mtime age >= 120s, which cannot distinguish 'finished' from 'SIGKILLed mid-write so mtime froze'.
ckpt_corruption_incident_20260810.eval_side_near_miss: the .82 watcher DID fire on the corrupt file at 00:49:54. It was stopped only by an unrelated 'REFUSE: 70424MiB held' (the A02 gate was using the GPUs). Luck, not design -- without that coincidence the headline 20k dose-point would have been computed from a 49% checkpoint.
ckpt_corruption_incident_20260810.fix: both watchers now require size == a known-good sibling ckpt AND size unchanged across two probes 60 s apart. Trainer side additionally replaced 'SIGTERM + kill -9 on a 20 s timer' with 'SIGTERM + poll up to 10 min', so a real save is never interrupted. Commits 8b53025 (trainer side) and 59ac8bc (eval side, also persists the watcher out of /tmp into code/a03_arm4_trajectory_watcher.sh).
